'''Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi Hime''' (遠津年魚眼眼妙媛, birth and death dates unknown) was an ancient figure in {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}.

== Genealogy ==

Her father was {{ill|Arakawato Hime|ja|荒河戸畔}}, a member of the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|lt=Kikoku no Miyatsuko}} clan. She became a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, bearing the children {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko}} and {{ill|Toyosukiiri-hime|ja|豊鍬入姫命}}.

== Scholarly Analysis ==

According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} and other sources, Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi Hime was listed as a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. She bore Prince {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko}}, whose royal succession eligibility was compared to his half-brother, Ikume no Mikoto, later known as {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}. However, it has been argued that the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|lt=Kikoku no Miyatsuko}} clan traditionally did not intermarry with the imperial family, raising questions about the historicity of this claim.<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男|lt=Hōga Toshio}}, "The Early Stages of the Keno Clan," in ''Studies on Ancient Clans XVII: The Keno Clan,'' Aogaki Publishing, 2021, pp. 31-33.</ref>

This theory posits that the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|ja|毛野氏|lt=Keno clan}} may have shared ancestry with the {{ill|Omononushi|ja|三輪君|lt=Miwa clan}}, evidenced by shared elements in naming conventions and religious practices, such as the worship of {{ill|Miwa deity|ja|三輪神}} and its widespread association with the {{ill|Raiden Shrine|ja|雷電神社}} network in the region. It has been suggested that the maternal lineage of {{ill|Mimorowake|ja|御諸別命|lt=Mimorowake-no-Mikoto}}, a descendant of the Keno clan, included a daughter of Arakawatobime.<ref>Hōga Toshio, "The Role of Keno and Related Clans in Ancient Japanese Society," in ''Studies on Ancient Clans XVII,'' Aogaki Publishing, 2021, pp. 55-77.</ref>

'''Tōtsu Ayumemaguwashi Hime''' (遠津年魚眼眼妙媛, birth and death dates unknown) was an ancient Japanese figure from the [[Kofun period]].
'''Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi-hime''' (遠津年魚眼眼妙媛, birth and death dates unknown) was an ancient {{ill|Japan|en|Japan|qid=Q17|lt=Japan}}ese figure from the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}.

== Genealogy ==
She was the daughter of {{ill|Arakawato Hime|ja|荒河戸畔}}, a member of the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造}}. She became a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}} and gave birth to {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko}} and {{ill|Toyosukiiri-hime|ja|豊鍬入姫命}}.

== Historical Analysis ==
In the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} and other sources, Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi-hime is described as a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, whose son, {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko}}, is compared with his half-brother {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850|lt=Ikume Iribiko Isachi}} in discussions of imperial succession. However, scholars note that it was not customary for women of the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造}} to enter the emperor's harem. Additionally, Ikume no Mikoto's mother, {{ill|Mimaki-hime|en|Mimaki-hime|qid=Q11071228|lt=Mimaki-hime}}, was an empress, making such a comparison unlikely.<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男}}, "2. The Early Stages of the Keno Clan: Issues Surrounding the Emergence of the Keno Lineage," in *Studies of Ancient Clans Vol. 17: The Keno Clan – The Origins of the Eastern Province's Prominent Lineage*, Aogaki Publishing, 2021, pp. 31–33.</ref>

According to the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, Tōtsu Ayumemaguwashi Hime was one of the consorts of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. She is credited with giving birth to {{ill|Prince Toyokiirihiko|ja|豊城入彦命|2=ja|3=豊城入彦命|qid=Q11633375|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyoki Iribiko no Mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Prince Toyokiirihiko}}, who is mentioned in a narrative comparing his potential for succession against his half-brother, {{ill|Ikume Iribiko no Mikoto|ja|活目尊}} (later {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}).

However, scholars question the credibility of this account. It has been noted that the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|fr|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko}} clan did not traditionally intermarry with the imperial family, and succession comparisons with Emperor Suinin, whose mother was Empress {{ill|Mimaki-hime|en|Mimaki-hime|qid=Q11071228|lt=Mimaki-hime}}, would not have been appropriate.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kōdai Shizoku no Kenkyū XVII: Keno-shi Higashi no Yūzoku Shobuke no Genryū|author=Toshio Hōga|publisher=Aogaki Shuppan|year=2021|pages=31–33}}</ref>

Some scholars argue that the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|ja|毛野氏|lt=Keno clan}}, which included the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|ja|上毛野氏}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno clan|ja|下毛野氏|lt=Shimotsukeno clan}}, was closely related to the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏}}. The {{ill|Miwa deity|ja|三輪神}} and associated rituals are prominent within the Keno clan's lineage, and similarities in surnames suggest a shared ancestry.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kōdai Shizoku no Kenkyū XVII: Keno-shi Higashi no Yūzoku Shobuke no Genryū|author=Toshio Hōga|publisher=Aogaki Shuppan|year=2021|pages=55–77}}</ref>

Despite doubts about her role as an imperial consort, connections between the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀氏|de|Ki (Klan)|uk|Рід Кі|ko|기씨 (황별)|fr|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt=Ki clan}} and {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏}} have been suggested, particularly through marriage alliances. Additionally, the presence of numerous shrines dedicated to {{ill|Raijin|en|Raijin|qid=Q12808082|lt=Raijin}}—a deity associated with the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|lt=Ki clan}}—in regions linked to the Keno clan further supports the hypothesis that Tōtsu Ayumemaguwashi Hime may have maternal ties to these groups.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kōdai Shizoku no Kenkyū XVII: Keno-shi Higashi no Yūzoku Shobuke no Genryū|author=Toshio Hōga|publisher=Aogaki Shuppan|year=2021|pages=55–77}}</ref>

{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男}} argues that the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|ja|毛野氏|lt=Keno clan}} (later associated with the provinces of {{ill|Kamitsuke no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|上毛野国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōzuke Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 上毛野国造|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11359471}} and {{ill|Shimotsukeno no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|下毛野国|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimotsuke Province|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 下毛野国造|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11361048}}) may have been related to the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏}}, citing similarities in clan surnames and evidence of {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|qid=Q705542|lt=Miwa Shrine}} worship among the Keno lineage. He also suggests that while Tōtsu Ayume Maguwashi-hime may not have been a consort of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}, it is plausible that her lineage connected with the maternal ancestry of {{ill|Mimorowake|ja|御諸別命|lt=Omimorowake no Mikoto}}, who was linked to both the {{ill|Kamitsukeno clan|ja|毛野氏|lt=Keno clan}} and the {{ill|Kii no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|紀国造|lt=Ki no Kuni clan}}. Supporting evidence includes the prominence of thunder deity worship in the Keno regions, such as at {{ill|Raijin Shrine|ja|雷神社|lt=Kaminari Shrines}}.<ref>{{ill|Toshio Hōga|ja|宝賀寿男}}, "2. The Early Stages of the Keno Clan: Issues Surrounding the Emergence of the Keno Lineage," in *Studies of Ancient Clans Vol. 17: The Keno Clan – The Origins of the Eastern Province's Prominent Lineage*, Aogaki Publishing, 2021, pp. 55–77.</ref>
